neighbours.label: Computer-aided design and manufacture: CAD, CNC and computer-controlled tools in engineering text; hand-tool versions and everyday computers stay low.
fire: The factory cuts its gears on CNC mills that follow a digital model.
Our draughtsmen moved to computer-aided drafting about twenty years ago.
Each bracket was modelled in SolidWorks and machined by a computer-controlled router.
The students design a chair in CAD and send it to the laser cutter.
Modern shipyards use computer-aided manufacturing to shape the steel plates.
The dentist's crown is milled from a block using CAD software and a scanner.
A Computer Numerical Control lathe turned the shafts to a tight tolerance.
Architects now produce the panels with parametric CAD models and robot arms.
quiet: The factory cuts its gears on old mills that follow a brass template.
Our draughtsmen moved to a larger office about twenty years ago.
Each bracket was sketched on paper and filed by an experienced fitter.
The students build a chair by hand and sand it with fine paper.
Older shipyards use teams of riveters to fix the steel plates.
The dentist's receptionist keeps the bills on a laptop and a small printer.
A home computer in the kitchen played the songs at low volume.
Architects now meet the clients in a bright studio with long tables.

predictions: 7/8 fire, 0-1 near miss. Hand-tool sentences reached up to 0.29 in probes.
notes: The output direction's top promoted tokens are ' computer' and variants. Probes: Computer Numerical Control 0.88, computer-aided 0.88, AutoCAD 0.59, FreeCAD 0.50, computer-controlled 0.48; computer science 0.01, buying a computer 0.00, simulation 0.07. So it isn't the word computer itself.
